_what_this_is: For every suffix that appears among ACTIVE, CLAIM-CAPABLE delivery surfaces but sits outside claim_auditor.SCANNED_SUFFIXES, a declared record naming exactly which claim class is covered elsewhere and which is not covered at all. scripts/claim_auditor.py --delivery-surfaces reads this and prints it at the point of use, and refuses to report a green result over a suffix with no record here.
_why: MEASURED 2026-08-17 at commit ba61911: the delivery inventory listed 108 active claim-capable surfaces and claim_auditor.scan_file returned scanned=False for 6 of them, because `main` filters the reports with `if r.scanned` and drops the rest without a word. The instrument N64 built to stop a green diff audit while an unchanged delivery surface carries an unsourced claim was reporting green over a population it could not read. That is measurement rule 4's blank gate and measurement rule 5's narrower-than-the-claim gate at once.
_why_not_just_widen_the_suffix_set: Because it was measured, on the real files, by toggling one variable on the real module. With .py and .yml added, action.yml produced 5 findings and scripts/cli.py produced 14, and almost all of them are ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM matching the verb `write` inside `write(f"` in shell and Python code. That is the same false-positive class N34 recorded when the regex read the tool name `Write` as an attribution verb. The auditor's unit is a prose paragraph with in-paragraph provenance; code and workflow files have neither, and the only ways to absorb the false positives would be the allowlist or the quarantine, both of which are prohibited as a way to make a check pass. The honest move is to state the coverage gap, not to scan blind and then suppress.
_rule: A record whose suffix appears in NO unscannable active claim-capable delivery surface FAILS AS STALE, following the discipline scripts/count_record_policy.py applies to not_a_count_claim and .claim-quarantine.json applies to its burn-downs: an exclusion must not outlive its premise. Declaring a suffix does not exempt a file from anything; it records who else is looking and what nobody is looking for.

covered_for: current output published without its qualifier
.yml.note: action.yml is a GitHub Action descriptor. Its `description` and step summaries are reader-facing on the Marketplace listing.

.toml.note: pyproject.toml's `description` and `keywords` are what PyPI renders on the project page, so they are read by more people than most site pages. NOTHING audits their content today. Measured 2026-08-17: the auditor finds 0 claims in it, so the gap is currently harmless and is recorded because a future edit to that description would not be seen by any claim instrument.

.py.note: scripts/cli.py and scripts/mcp_server.py are claim-capable because argparse help text and MCP tool descriptions are printed to users. Measured 2026-08-17: scanning scripts/cli.py with the auditor surfaces `200 KB` and `12 months` in help text as genuine numeric claims, alongside twelve ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM false positives on the verb `write`. The two genuine ones are recorded here rather than fixed, because sourcing a help string is a user-facing change that requires its own review.

.json.note: site/sa-tracker.json is regulatory tracker data served to the browser. Measured 2026-08-17: the auditor finds 2 claims and 0 unsourced in it, so widening to .json would be inert today; it is left out because the auditor's paragraph unit does not exist in JSON and a green result from a unit that cannot apply is not evidence.

.xml.note: site/sitemap.xml contains <loc> URLs and <lastmod> dates and no prose. Measured 2026-08-17: the auditor finds 0 claims in it. This is a declared EMPTY coverage entry rather than a silent omission: no instrument reads it, and the reason it is acceptable is that its grammar has nowhere to put a claim, not that anybody checked.
